raw_response:
I will keep my land in the crop pattern that fits Quzhou best: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. I farm for steady grain and lower risk, so I will not scatter my land into many small crops. In my place, wheat and maize match the climate, the machinery, and the market, and I know how to manage them. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, put most of my fertilizer into wheat before and during early growth, irrigate wheat more because spring is dry, and give maize fewer irrigations because summer rain usually helps. I will plough before wheat to leave a good seedbed after maize, then use rotary tillage before maize after the wheat harvest so I can turn the field around quickly. I will watch weeds, aphids, rust, armyworm, and corn borers, spray only when pressure is clear, and aim for stable yield rather than chasing the absolute highest output.
